A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MambaTM and latent phase distortion study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete supplementary material are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration benchmarks, computational measurements, ablations and real-world qualitative results in Section 4 and supplementary Sections 8–9.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds KL-weight sensitivity results and a BRIAR face-retrieval evaluation before and after semi-supervised fine-tuning.

M1.justification: Section 4.6 adds mean-teacher semi-supervised fine-tuning, using an exponentially averaged teacher as the final model. This extends the training procedure while retaining the MambaTM architecture, LPD/ReBlurNet components and original supervised losses.

E1.justification: BRIAR already supplied qualitative examples in v1. v2 additionally uses real-world BRIAR Research clips for training and evaluates human-face retrieval on BRIAR Testing, extending training coverage and downstream task coverage. The existing benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding restoration benchmarks, qualitative comparisons and computational-cost table. The added studies compare MambaTM configurations and fine-tuning status; the newly cited person-recognition model serves as the downstream evaluator.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a four-value KL-weight sweep and a 60,000-step fine-tuning protocol with learning rate 0.0001, batch size 1 and equal proportions of synthetic and real-world videos. It adds rank-20 face-retrieval evaluation. Earlier experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds KL-weight sensitivity analysis on ATSyn-static and ATSyn-dynamic, plus a real-world visualization of the blur representation. Section 4.6 measures the effect of fine-tuning. Earlier architecture, scanning, LPD-guidance and temporal-extrapolation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for these comparisons. The new discussion of sigma maps concerns the existing latent representation; experimental uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Shared numerical results are unchanged. New Table 7 reports results under additional KL weights, including ATSyn-dynamic PSNR 30.0189 at weight 0.01. New Table 8 reports face-retrieval accuracy before versus after fine-tuning: 78.4% versus 78.8% overall, 85.0% versus 86.4% on LR Face, and 71.4% versus 72.5% on LR Turb.

T1.justification: The turbulence-model, variational-loss and state-space mathematics, including supplementary Section 7.1, are retained. The added teacher-update equation specifies the training extension; no new theoretical result, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain their central contributions and performance claims. The conclusion adds the potential to separate degradation from scene content, while qualifying that this prospect concerns the learned blur representation and does not yet extend to tilt.

C2.justification: v2 links KL regularization to scene independence, discusses instability above KL weight 0.01, and explains the trivial identity solution motivating mean-teacher fine-tuning. It also explicitly identifies scene-dependent tilt as a limitation. These extend the earlier interpretation of LPD.

D1.justification: Section 4.6 documents the selection of over 10,000 BRIAR clips, fine-tuning hyperparameters, teacher averaging coefficient 0.999 and final teacher-model selection. The abstract also replaces the direct code-repository pointer with a project-page pointer. Earlier implementation details remain.

R1.justification: v2 retains all 102 earlier references and adds three works supporting the new fine-tuning section: Person Recognition at Altitude and Range, Kernel Diffusion, and Mean Teachers. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammar and terminology corrections, adds a KL-loss discussion and Section 4.6, and expands the conclusion. The existing narrative organization and supplementary sections are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a six-panel real-world LPD figure and two compact results tables. Existing visual content and table designs are retained, with modest reflow and renumbering: supplementary Figures 5–8 become 6–9, and Tables 7–8 become 9–10.

improvement.justification: The KL-weight study, documented real-world fine-tuning experiment and explicit tilt limitation improve empirical support and transparency. These are useful extensions to the retained evidence. The face-retrieval gains are modest and lack uncertainty estimates, so the additions support a limited overall improvement rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper.
